text:
ellie-recruiter: Hey @sara-peopleops — hiring update: candidate for Backend SDE (London, remote-first) needs a Skilled Worker visa. Target start 2026-05-02. Can we sponsor and what do we need from them? Also: can payroll set up tax & benefits before BRP arrives?

sara-peopleops: Hi @ellie-recruiter — yes we can sponsor if role & salary meet Skilled Worker rules. Quick checklist first: are they currently in the UK or overseas? Do they already have a CoS with another sponsor?

ellie-recruiter: They're currently in India, accepting our offer next week. No existing CoS. Salary offered is £52,000.

sara-peopleops: salary and role look fine (above going-rate threshold). Next steps: we issue a CoS once signed offer returned, then candidate applies for visa. Timeline is typically 4–8 weeks from application (depends on local VAC). We should plan start date with 8–10 weeks buffer.

sara-peopleops: Company covers Home Office application fee + Immigration lawyer basic package per policy. Candidate pays Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) at application, we reimburse after visa grant (submit receipts).

natascha-legal: a couple of legal bits — ensure SOC code + job duties are accurate on the CoS, and that salary components are structured per guidance (fixed salary + bonuses cannot undercut the qualifying salary). Also we need the job advert history if asked. I can review the draft CoS before issuance.

ryan-payroll: Payroll notes: we can provisionally create a UK payroll record without a National Insurance number, but we need:
- bank details
- passport photo page copy
- home address in UK (or provisional UK address for BRP collection)
- expected start date
If they don't have a NI yet, tax code will default to "BR" until HMRC issues their code — that means emergency tax may apply. We can apply to HMRC for a tax code after submission, but it takes time. Please ask candidate for P45 only if they were employed in the UK previously.

ellie-recruiter: BRP pickup question — candidate will enter UK on 30-day vignette. Where do we put the postal pickup address? Company HQ or candidate home?

sara-peopleops: Put candidate's UK residential address (recommended) so it's convenient for them. If they don't have one yet, we can use a temporary address (team lead's address only with consent). Candidate will need passport vignette to enter and then collect BRP within 10 days of arrival. See gov.uk: https://www.gov.uk/biometric-residence-permits

visa-bot: Reminder: Required docs list for CoS/visa app — please upload scanned copies to the secure intake folder.

```
Required docs for CoS + payroll provisioning:
- Passport (photo page)
- Digital passport photo (for BRP where requested)
- Degree certificates (if listed as qualification)
- Proof of address (if UK address available; else provisional)
- Signed offer + start date
- Bank details (UK or international for initial setup)
```

ellie-recruiter: Thanks. Two policy Qs from candidate: 1) relocation stipend timing (pay out vs. reimbursement)? 2) benefits enrollment — can they enroll before BRP/NI arrives?

sara-peopleops: Relocation stipend: we can front a lump-sum on first payroll run (treat as taxable relocation). For company moves we sometimes reimburse on receipt. Confirm in offer letter. Benefits: we can enroll them in basic benefits (pension auto-enrolment) from day 1, but we need NI to finalize contributions. Some voluntary benefits (private medical) need ID verification — we can temporarily enroll and finalize once BRP/NI present.

natascha-legal: add-on: ensure internal cost codes for CoS fee + legal are attached to the requisition so finance can process the vendor.

ryan-payroll: Operational ask: please open a People Ops ticket with subject "UK Skilled Worker — <candidate name>" and attach scanned docs at least 5 working days before start. We'll set up payroll and flag tax team to request HMRC tax code.

ellie-recruiter: Got it. I'll create the ticket and upload scans tonight. Candidate confirmed they'll apply for visa next Monday. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
